blocks.heading: Engineered for the wheelset, built for the workshop
paragraphs: Every railway vehicle depends on its wheelsets. Their profile governs ride quality, rail wear and derailment safety; their geometry decides whether a train may run at all. HYT Engineering has concentrated on this subject since 1977, and the product range reflects it: machines that restore, build, measure and balance wheelsets, plus the depot equipment that keeps maintenance flowing.

Every machine is designed in-house in Pune and adapted to the customer's track gauge, wheel profiles and vehicle types. Where one machine is not enough, we combine several into a complete facility through our [turnkey projects](page:turnkey-project) – and support them for their working life through our [service organisation](page:services).

blocks.heading: How to choose the right wheel lathe
blocks.intro: The right machine depends less on the wheel than on your operation. Six questions narrow the choice quickly.

items.title: Does the wheelset stay in the vehicle?
items.text: To re-profile without dropping bogies, choose an underfloor lathe. If wheelsets are removed anyway during overhaul, a surface or portal lathe fits that flow.

items.title: How many wheelsets per day?
items.text: Fleet size and re-profiling interval set the workload. High-utilisation metro and EMU fleets often justify a tandem machine that handles a whole bogie in one setting.

items.title: What civil works are possible?
items.text: Underfloor lathes need a reinforced pit beneath the track. Surface and portal lathes work on removed wheelsets and need no pit under a running line – often simpler in an existing building.

items.title: Which wheel sizes and gauges?
items.text: List the smallest and largest tread diameters, axle lengths and gauges in your fleet, including vehicles you expect to buy. The machine is sized to that envelope.

items.title: Brake discs as well?
items.text: Wheel- and axle-mounted brake discs can be machined on suitable configurations. Tell us early, because it affects tooling and machine layout.

items.title: Stand-alone or part of a line?
items.text: Linked with [measuring stations](page:wheel-measuring-station) and wheelset handling, a lathe can become part of an [automated wheel shop](page:ts-wheel-shops#automation). Plan the interfaces from the start.

blocks.heading: Re-profiling at floor level
paragraphs: Many workshops remove wheelsets from the vehicle anyway – during bogie overhaul, after a wheel change or when axleboxes and bearings are serviced. For them, machining in a pit beneath the track brings no benefit. A surface wheel lathe does the job at floor level, where the wheelset is easy to reach, inspect and handle.

The wheelset is rolled into the machine on rails, raised into the machining position and clamped. Both wheels are measured and turned to the specified profile, and suitable configurations also machine wheel- or axle-mounted brake discs in the same setting.

**Surface or underfloor?** An [underfloor wheel lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe) re-profiles wheels while the wheelset stays in the vehicle. That saves dismantling, but it needs a pit under the track. A surface lathe needs no pit and suits workshops where wheelsets come out of the vehicle in the normal course of maintenance, or where the building does not allow civil works beneath the rails.

items.q: What is the difference between a surface and an underfloor wheel lathe?
items.a: A surface lathe stands at floor level and machines wheelsets that have been removed from the vehicle. An [underfloor lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe) works in a pit beneath the track and machines the wheelset while it stays in the vehicle.

items.q: Which model should I choose?
items.a: Start with your largest tread diameter, longest axle and heaviest wheelset. The YSL-08 covers tread diameters up to 1250 mm and wheelsets up to 50 kN. Data for the YSL-12 and YSL-21 is supplied on request, together with our recommendation.

items.q: Can brake discs be machined?
items.a: Yes, on suitable configurations. The YSL-08 machines brake discs from 250 to 700 mm in diameter in the same setting as the wheels.

items.q: What foundation is needed?
items.a: A level, reinforced foundation at floor level, sized to the machine. No pit under the track is required. HYT provides the foundation drawing early in the project.

items.q: Should I choose a surface or a portal lathe?
items.a: Both machine removed wheelsets. A [portal wheel lathe](page:portal-wheel-lathe) is built around a rigid portal frame for heavy cuts in continuous wheel-shop production. A surface lathe suits depots and overhaul shops that re-profile wheelsets and brake discs alongside other overhaul work. We recommend one or the other after reviewing your workload.

blocks.heading: Wheel maintenance without taking the train apart
paragraphs: Flats, hollow treads and thin flanges are a fact of railway life. The traditional remedy – dropping the bogie, pulling the wheelset and sending it to the wheel shop – costs days of availability and a great deal of labour. The YUL-08 brings the machine to the wheelset instead.

Installed in a pit beneath a straight section of track, the lathe lifts the axle off the rails on its own drive rollers, clamps the axlebox securely and machines both wheels at the same time. Brake gear, traction motors and bogie frames stay where they are. When the cycle ends, the wheelset is lowered back on to the rails and the next axle is positioned over the machine.
Because the vehicle stays coupled and assembled, one YUL-08 can keep a large fleet within profile limits and shorten the time each train spends out of service.

items.a: No. The YUL-08 machines the wheelset while it remains in the bogie. Brake gear, traction motors and axleboxes stay in place.

blocks.heading: Two wheelsets, one setting
paragraphs: On a single underfloor lathe, the wheelsets of a bogie are machined one after the other: the vehicle is moved, the next axle is positioned and the cycle starts again. The YUL-12T removes that step. Two machines installed in one pit work in synchronised tandem, so both wheelsets of a bogie are re-profiled together.

One unit is fixed; the second traverses along the pit to suit the bogie wheelbase. A single installation can therefore serve vehicles with different bogie designs – from locomotives to coaches and multiple units – without changes to the foundation.

HYT figures show that tandem operation reduces re-profiling time by 50% for coaches and 33% for locomotives compared with a single machine. For a platform positioned for higher automation, compare the [YUGLX](page:tandem-underfloor-wheel-lathe-yuglx).

blocks.heading: Journal finishing, not full axle turning
paragraphs: Every wheelset overhaul brings the axle journals under scrutiny. Corrosion, fretting marks and wear at the bearing seats must be removed, and the journal returned to a diameter and surface finish that the bearing specification accepts.

The CNC Axle Journal Turning & Burnishing Lathe is built for exactly that task. It turns the journal and adjacent seats to size, then burnishes the surface: hardened rollers press down the peaks left by turning and leave a smooth, compacted finish. Burnishing is a cold-working process – it produces no chips.
**This is an overhaul machine.** For turning complete axles from raw or forged blanks in new production, see the [CNC Axle Turning Lathe ATL-01](page:axle-turning-lathe).

items.q: Why burnish after turning?

wheel-presses.description: HYT wheel presses mount and dismount railway wheels on axles with controlled hydraulic force – for accurate, traceable press-fits in wheel and axle shops.
wheel-presses.h1: Wheel Press for mounting and dismounting railway wheelsets
wheel-presses.lede: Wheels are held on their axles by an interference fit, not by fasteners. A wheel press makes and breaks that fit under controlled force – and the quality of the joint depends on it.

blocks.heading: Making and breaking the interference fit
paragraphs: A railway wheel is pressed on to its axle seat with a specified interference: the bore is slightly smaller than the seat. During mounting, the force rises as the wheel travels along the seat, and that force profile shows whether the joint is sound.

HYT wheel presses are built for both directions of this work. In mounting, the press positions the wheel and drives it on to the seat to the specified back-to-back distance. In dismounting, it applies the force needed to remove worn wheels from axles that will be reused.

Pressing brings together the work of other wheel-shop machines: bores from the [vertical turning and boring machine](page:vertical-turning-boring-machine), seats from the [axle turning lathe](page:axle-turning-lathe) and final checks on the [wheel measuring station](page:wheel-measuring-station).

dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.title: Dynamic Wheel Balancing Machine for Railway Wheels
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.description: HYT dynamic wheel balancing machine measures the unbalance of railway wheels and wheelsets in rotation, so it can be corrected for smoother, quieter running.
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.h1: Dynamic Wheel Balancing Machine for railway wheels and wheelsets
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.lede: An unbalanced wheel vibrates at every revolution, loading bearings and track and reducing ride comfort. The balancing machine measures how much unbalance there is and where, so it can be corrected before service.
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.summary: Measures the dynamic unbalance of railway wheels and wheelsets so it can be corrected before service – for smoother running and longer component life.

blocks.heading: Why balance matters as speed rises
paragraphs: Unbalance is mass that is not evenly distributed around the axis of rotation. At low speed its effect is small. The resulting force, however, grows with the square of speed, and an unbalanced wheel becomes a source of vibration for bearings, bogie, track and car body.

A dynamic balancing machine spins the wheel or wheelset and measures the forces this creates. It determines both the amount and the angular position of the unbalance, in one or two planes, so the workshop knows exactly how much material to remove or add, and where.
Operators of passenger trains, metros and multiple units commonly specify balance limits for their wheels, because ride comfort, noise and component life depend on them.

multi-purpose-armature-machine.description: HYT multipurpose armature machine for traction-motor overhaul: commutator turning, mica undercutting and related armature operations on one machine.
multi-purpose-armature-machine.h1: Multipurpose Armature Machine for traction-motor armature maintenance
multi-purpose-armature-machine.lede: Traction-motor armatures need several precision operations during overhaul. This machine brings them together, so the armature is moved and set up fewer times.

blocks.heading: Restoring the commutator, keeping motors in service
paragraphs: In a DC traction motor, current reaches the armature through the commutator and carbon brushes. Over time the commutator wears out of round, its surface roughens and the mica insulation between the copper segments ends up level with the copper. The results are rapid brush wear, sparking and, eventually, motor failure.

Restoring the commutator involves several operations: turning the surface true, undercutting the mica below the copper and finishing the segment edges. The multipurpose armature machine performs these operations on one machine, so the armature moves between workstations less often.
The exact range of functions is configured to the armature types in your fleet.

blocks.heading: Shunting without tying up a locomotive
paragraphs: Depots and workshops move vehicles all day: on to the wheel lathe road, through the washing plant, over inspection pits and out to the stabling sidings. Using a locomotive for each move ties up traction and crew, and a locomotive cannot leave the rails to reach a different track.

A Rail cum Road Vehicle (Shunter) can. It drives on the road on its tyres, sets down its rail guide wheels at a track access point and then runs on the rails to couple and move rolling stock. When the job is done, it raises the rail wheels and drives to the next track.
Coupling system, braking, hauling capacity and gauge are matched to the vehicles you need to move and the layout of your depot.

items.q: What is a rail cum road vehicle?
items.a: A vehicle that can drive on roads on its tyres and run on rails using retractable guide wheels. In shunting mode it couples to rolling stock and moves it along the track.

items.q: How many vehicles can it move?
items.a: That depends on the configured hauling capacity, the weight of your rolling stock and the gradients in the depot. We size the vehicle to your heaviest regular movement.

items.q: What infrastructure does it need?

blocks.heading: Why sliding surfaces matter
paragraphs: Wherever a heavy part moves along a guide – a machine slide, a table, a carriage or a ram – the sliding surface decides how smoothly, accurately and quietly it moves, and how long it lasts. Friction, stick-slip and wear in these surfaces translate directly into lost accuracy and extra maintenance.

"Gleittechnik" is German for sliding technology, and it is SKC Gleittechnik's field. HYT Engineering is the company's exclusive distributor in India, combining the partner's products with our own experience as a builder and servicer of heavy machine tools.
Whether you are building new machines, reconditioning worn slideways or upgrading existing equipment, HYT advises on where sliding technology fits and coordinates supply with SKC.
